question: After repeated encounters with one partner's flight, does a research fly's escape response to that partner change, and is any change specific to that partner?

hypotheses.H1: Repeated encounters reduce escape: P(escape | familiar test) is lower than P(escape | first encounter). Supported when the 95% Newcombe interval of familiar − naive lies wholly below 0.
hypotheses.H2: The change is specific to the partner: after the same series, P(escape | stranger test) is higher than P(escape | familiar test). Supported when the interval of stranger − familiar lies wholly above 0, the manipulation check passes and the stretches are balanced.
hypotheses.H3: The change outlasts a long delay: P(escape | familiar test after the long delay) is lower than P(escape | first encounter). Supported when the interval of familiar-late − naive lies wholly below 0.
